name: IS31FL3731-QFLS2-TR
title: IS31FL3731: audio-modulated 144-LED matrix driver with I2C
summary: An I2C-controlled driver for up to 144 single LEDs, arranged as two cross-plexed 9-line matrices of 72 that need only 18 pins. Every LED has its own on/off bit, blink bit and 8-bit PWM value. Eight frames are stored on chip and can be shown as a still picture, played as an animation with breathing fades, or stepped by an audio input that can also modulate brightness. Runs from 2.7 V to 5.5 V, -40 °C to +85 °C, in QFN-28 (4 mm × 4 mm) or SSOP-28; IS31FL3731-QFLS2-TR is the QFN on reel.
key_figures: 3.2 mA typ at REXT = 20 kΩ (ILED = 64.7 / REXT)
I2C, 400 kHz, four addresses by AD

circuits.title: Typical application: 144-LED matrix
circuits.description: A 144-LED display. VCC runs from VBattery with 1 µF and 0.1 µF to ground. A microcontroller drives SDA and SCL, reads INTB and holds SDB; SDA, SCL and INTB are each pulled up to the logic supply VDD by 4.7 kΩ, and SDB is pulled to ground by 100 kΩ. Audio comes in through 0.22 µF to IN. A 20 kΩ REXT sets 3.2 mA average per LED, C_FILT has 0.1 µF to ground, and AD is grounded. Matrix A hangs on CA1-CA9 and matrix B on CB1-CB9: LED Cx-y has its cathode on line x of its matrix and its anode on line y (counting within the matrix) when y < x, or on line y+1 when y >= x, so each line is a cathode for eight LEDs and an anode for the others.
notes: Keep the IC well away from a phone's antenna to avoid EMI.
Each LED averages 3.2 mA with REXT = 20 kΩ; REXT scales it (ILED = 64.7 / REXT).
The thermal pad of the QFN goes to GND.
The LED labels Cx-y are the LED positions addressed by the frame registers.

operation.text: Two matrices of 72 LEDs each, A on CA1-CA9 and B on CB1-CB9, give 144 LEDs from 18 lines by cross-plexing. The nine lines are scanned in turn at 1/9 duty: each scan slot lasts 106 µs typ, with 15 µs typ of blanking between slots, and column data loads on each rising edge.

Standard I2C up to 400 kHz. The 7-bit address is 11101 followed by two bits set by the AD pin (GND 00, VCC 11, SCL 01, SDA 10); the eighth bit is R/W. SDA is open drain and needs a pull-up, typically 4.7 kΩ. A write is: address, register address, then data, MSB first, each byte acknowledged by the chip. The register pointer advances by one after each data byte, so a burst write fills consecutive registers.

All registers are readable. Frame registers can be read only in software shutdown with SDB high; the function registers can be read in shutdown or in operation. A read writes FDh with the number of the wanted page, restarts, writes the register address, restarts again with R/W = 1 and then clocks the data out.

Writing the Command Register at FDh selects one of nine pages: 00h-07h are Frames 1-8, each holding LED on/off (00h-11h), blink enable (12h-23h) and PWM (24h-B3h) for all 144 LEDs; 0Bh is the function page with the mode, playback, breath, audio and shutdown controls. Frame contents are random at power-up.

Each LED has an 8-bit PWM register, 256 linear steps of brightness. Rewriting the PWM values steadily produces a breathing effect. For smoother-looking fades a gamma table maps fewer intensity steps onto PWM values: 32 steps are the standard set, 64 steps are recommended; 32 steps suit a 1 s breathing cycle and 64 steps a 2 s cycle, and the final choice depends on the LED and the look of the product.
MODE = 00. One frame, chosen by PFS in register 01h, is shown. Breathing can be added through register 09h.

MODE = 01. The eight stored frames play in order starting at the frame set by FS. Register 02h sets the number of loops and frames, 03h the delay between frames, and 08h/09h the breathing between frames. With FS = 011, CNS = 011 and FNS = 011 the movie plays frames 4 to 6 three times and stops on frame 7.
MODE = 1x. The audio level, sampled at the rate set in 0Ch, picks which of the eight frames is shown: the quietest level shows frame 1, the loudest frame 8.
Setting AE in 06h makes the audio input scale the intensity of the LEDs, on top of each LED's PWM setting. Gain from 0 to 21 dB in 3 dB steps, and slow or fast AGC, are set in 0Bh.
With BE in 05h set, each LED whose blink bit is set in its frame blinks with period BPT at 50% duty.
When the shown frame changes, B_EN in 09h turns on a fade sequence: the frame holds for FDT, fades out over FOT, stays dark for ET, and the next frame fades in over FIT.

In Auto Frame Play Mode INTB is high and INT is 0 while the movie plays. At the end INTB goes low and INT becomes 1. INTB returns high by itself after staying low for at least 7 ms; INT clears only when register 07h is read.

Any subset of the 144 positions can be fitted, for example a matrix A without C9-3 to C9-5 and C5-8 to C9-8. Positions with no LED must be switched off in the LED control registers, otherwise they disturb the LEDs that are fitted.
For longer animations, load all eight frames, play frames 1-4, then play 5-8 while rewriting 1-4, then play the new 1-4 while rewriting 5-8, using the end-of-play interrupt to pace each half.

Registers keep their contents in either shutdown. Software shutdown (SSD = 0 in 0Ah) turns off all current sources and digital drivers and blanks the matrix; with SDB high the registers can still be written and read, and supply current is 230 µA typ. Hardware shutdown, SDB low, blocks all register access and draws 0.5 µA typ, 5 µA max.
Place the IC far from a phone's antenna to prevent EMI. The QFN thermal pad goes to GND.
